'''Ben James Winer''' (June 18, 1917 &ndash; May 30, 1984) was an American research psychologist and academic. He served as a psychology professor at [[Purdue University]] and was president of the [[Psychometric Society]]. He has been listed as one of the most highly cited psychologists in the United States, having authored a well-known textbook on statistical analysis.

==Biography==
Born in Oregon, Winer attended the [[University of Oregon]] and he served as a personnel research bureau assistant for the psychology department head, Howard Taylor.<ref name="Eugene">{{cite news|title=Elizabeth DeBusk wins job as assistant|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1310&dat=19390818&id=Ga9WAAAAIBAJ&pg=4427,1964911&hl=en|access-date=February 9, 2016|work=[[Eugene Register-Guard]]|date=August 18, 1939}}</ref> He earned a master's degree in psychology from Oregon in 1940 before serving in the military for five years. He held positions with the [[United States Civil Service Commission]] and [[The Pentagon]] while he took evening graduate courses in statistics at [[George Washington University]].<ref name=AmPsych/>

After briefly attending graduate school at [[Princeton University]], Winer went to [[Ohio State University]], where he earned a Ph.D. in [[industrial and organizational psychology|industrial psychology]] in 1951.<ref name=AmPsych>{{cite journal|title=Distinguished Teaching of Quantitative Methods in Psychology Award|journal=[[American Psychologist]]|date=March 1984|volume=39|issue=3|pages=313–314|url=https://www.psychometricsociety.org/sites/default/files/Ben_J_Winer_from_Purdue.pdf|access-date=February 9, 2016}}</ref> He was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of North Carolina]] and he received joint teaching appointments in statistics and psychology at [[Purdue University]] in 1954. He had a full-time appointment in the psychology department by 1956, but statistical analysis remained a strong area of emphasis for him.<ref name=AmPsych/> Working with Andrew Halpin, Winer studied behavioral approaches to leadership. They concluded that two concepts, ''initiating structure'' and ''consideration'', characterized the behavior of successful leadership.<ref name="Daresh">{{cite book|last1=Daresh|first1=John|title=Leading and Supervising Instruction|date=2006|publisher=[[Corwin Press]]|isbn=978-1-4833-3415-8|page=38|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Cd8hAQAAQBAJ&pg=PA38|access-date=February 9, 2016}}</ref>

Winer was the 1967-68 president of the [[Psychometric Society]].<ref name="Psychometric">{{cite web|title=Past, present and incoming presidents|url=https://www.psychometricsociety.org/content/past-present-and-incoming-presidents|publisher=[[Psychometric Society]]|access-date=February 6, 2016}}</ref> In 1983, he received a Quantitative Methods Teaching Award from the [[American Psychological Association|American Psychological Foundation]]. He authored an influential textbook, ''Statistical Principles in Experimental Design''.<ref name="TOP">{{cite journal|title=News tips from ToP|journal=Teaching of Psychology|date=October 1983|volume=10|issue=3|page=192|doi=10.1207/s15328023top1003_31|s2cid=220606414}}</ref> The book was reviewed in journals including ''[[Educational and Psychological Measurement]]'',<ref name="Wiley">{{cite journal|last1=Wiley|first1=D. E.|title=Book Reviews: Statistical Principles in Experimental Design by B. J. Winer. New York: McGraw-Hill Book Company, Inc., 1962. Pp. x + 672. $12.50|journal=Educational and Psychological Measurement|date=1 April 1963|volume=23|issue=1|pages=205–207|doi=10.1177/001316446302300122|s2cid=145734196|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/247725034|access-date=February 9, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Wasik">{{cite journal|last1=Wasik|first1=J. L.|title=Book Reviews: B. J. Winer. Statistical Principles in Experimental Design. (2nd. ed.). New York: McGraw-Hill, 1971, pp. xx + 907. $16.50|journal=Educational and Psychological Measurement|date=1 July 1972|volume=32|issue=2|pages=537–539|doi=10.1177/001316447203200249|s2cid=144974612|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/247725998|access-date=February 9, 2016}}</ref> ''Ergonomics''<ref name="Wyon">{{cite journal|last1=Wyon|first1=D. P.|title=A review of Statistical Principles in Experimental Design, 2nd Edition, By B. J. Winer. (New York: McGraw-Hill, 1971.) [Pp. xv+907.]|journal=Ergonomics|date=July 1972|volume=15|issue=4|pages=479–481|doi=10.1080/00140137208928244}}</ref> and the ''[[Journal of the American Statistical Association]]''.<ref name="JASA">{{cite journal|last1=Geisser|first1=Seymour|title=Book Reviews|journal=Journal of the American Statistical Association|date=December 1963|volume=58|issue=304|pages=1164–1204|doi=10.1080/01621459.1963.10480696}}</ref> In 2002, Winer was ranked fourth on a list of American psychologists most frequently cited in the professional literature;<ref name="Top100">{{cite journal|last1=Haggbloom|first1=Steven J.|last2=Warnick|first2=Renee|last3=Warnick|first3=Jason E.|last4=Jones|first4=Vinessa K.|last5=Yarbrough|first5=Gary L.|last6=Russell|first6=Tenea M.|last7=Borecky|first7=Chris M.|last8=McGahhey|first8=Reagan|last9=Powell|first9=John L. III|last10=Beavers|first10=Jamie|last11=Monte|first11=Emmanuelle|title=The 100 most eminent psychologists of the 20th century|journal=[[Review of General Psychology]]|date=2002|volume=6|issue=2|pages=139–152|doi=10.1037/1089-2680.6.2.139|url=http://creativity.ipras.ru/texts/top100.pdf|access-date=February 6, 2016|s2cid=145668721}}</ref> ''Statistical Principles in Experimental Design'' remains his most cited work by far.<ref name="Index">{{cite news|last1=Roediger|first1=Henry L.|title=The h index in science: A new measure of scholarly contribution|url=http://www.psychologicalscience.org/index.php/publications/observer/2006/april-06/the-h-index-in-science-a-new-measure-of-scholarly-contribution.html|work=Observer|agency=[[Association for Psychological Science]]|date=April 2006}}</ref>

Upon his death, Winer left a gift to Purdue to further the study of [[mathematical psychology]]. The university established a memorial lecture series in his honor.<ref name="Dzhafarov">{{cite book|last1=Dzhafarov|first1=Ehtibar|last2=Perry|first2=Lacey (eds.)|title=Descriptive and normative approaches to human behavior|date=2012|publisher=World Scientific|location=New Jersey|isbn=978-981-4368-01-8|page=v|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=P166CgAAQBAJ&pg=PR5|access-date=February 6, 2016}}</ref> A distinguished professorship at the school was named after him in 1998.<ref name="PurdueNews">{{cite web|title=Distinguished profs named on basis of teaching|url=https://www.purdue.edu/uns/html4ever/1998/980904.BOT.Disting.teach.html|publisher=[[Purdue University]]|access-date=February 6, 2016|date=September 4, 1998}}</ref>
